# mc_rtc encounters sporadic 10 ms calculation peaks during 5 ms control cycle, which were verified through three diagnostic measures?

> **Current answer:** The project members recommended verifying three items: setting the LogPolicy of mc_rtc to threaded; ensuring that the lipm_walking controller and lipm_walking_controller and all dependencies are built with Release or RelWithDebInfo; and disabling CPU powersaving. The author applied these three changes and confirmed a significant reduction in both peak and total execution time. The project members also noted that state initialization can still cause peaks, and these are only tolerable in cases where deadline misses are rare; they do not claim this is a hard real-time fix. The applicability applies to the original post 2020 mc_rtc/LIPM, ROS, and 5 ms entity robot control loop; other versions and controllers should be re-measured. ## Key terms

- Real-time jitter (实时抖动)
- Control deadline (控制截止时间)
- Threaded logging policy (线程化日志策略)
- Release build (发布构建)

## Problem and symptoms

- When the mc_rtc and LIPM controller run at 5 ms intervals, the calculation time occasionally rises to about 10 ms, and how to reduce real-time jitter?
- A sporadic peak in perf records, with calculation time exceeding 5 ms deadline and reaching about 10 ms.

## Environment

- 2020 mc_rtc and LIPM controller; ROS; entity robot; 5 ms sampling time; CPU and software versions not specified.

## Priority diagnostics

- The peak was checked to occur simultaneously with the state initialization.
- The LogPolicy, controllers, and all dependencies were verified for their build types and CPU power-saving status.

## Possible causes

- The default non-threaded logging policy may introduce significant peaks.
- Controllers or any single dependency not built with an optimized build, and CPU power-saving, all of which can amplify the execution time; state switching allocation itself can also generate peaks.

## Attempts

- The author set the LogPolicy of mc_rtc to threaded and verified the relevant controllers and dependencies with Release/RelWithDebInfo, and disabled CPU powersaving.

## Effective fixes

- A threaded LogPolicy was used; all dependencies of lipm_walking controller and lipm_walking_controller were built with Release or RelWithDebInfo; CPU powersaving was disabled.

## Result

- The three adjustments significantly reduced both peak and total execution time.

## Limitations

- The individual contributions of the three measures were not quantified, and the adjusted worst-case execution time was not provided.
- The project members only mentioned the system's tolerance for rare deadline misses; this is not a hard real-time or all systems safe guarantee.
- The peak during state initialization is still considered a problem that needs improvement in future versions.

## Safety notes

- Measurements of the worst-case execution time and deadline miss frequency should still be taken before deploying to an entity robot, and these should be handled by the target system's safety mechanism.
